title: Running Config vs Startup Config
description: Understand the difference between running-config and startup-config and how to manage both.
scenario: Understand the difference between running-config and startup-config and how to manage both.

steps.title: Look at the live config
steps.instruction: The switch boots from what is saved in NVRAM, so right now RAM and NVRAM hold exactly the same thing. Prove it — read the active config.

steps.title: Read the saved copy
steps.instruction: Same file, different home. This is the startup-config from NVRAM — identical to the running-config, because you have not changed anything yet.

steps.buttonLabel: Add a VLAN on the switch
steps.title: Make a change in the topology editor
steps.instruction: Now add a configuration: VLAN 20 on FastEthernet0/3. Click the button and watch it type itself into the terminal.
steps.hint: Step 3 wants: the Add a VLAN on the switch button

steps.title: The running-config changed
steps.instruction: There it is — vlan 20 and the Fa0/3 line. This is the whole point of RAM: changes work immediately, with no reboot.

steps.title: …but the saved copy did not
steps.instruction: Still the old config. NVRAM knows nothing about VLAN 20 — pull the power and that change is gone forever.

steps.title: Save it to NVRAM
steps.instruction: Push RAM into NVRAM. This is the command people forget — and the one that costs them a weekend.

steps.title: Now both copies match
steps.instruction: VLAN 20 is in the saved copy too, so it survives a reboot. running-config = RAM, startup-config = NVRAM, write memory = the bridge between them.

concepts.title: Running Config
concepts.body: The running-config is the active configuration stored in RAM. Changes take effect immediately.
concepts.code:
SW1# show running-config
! Active configuration — lives in RAM

concepts.title: Startup Config
concepts.body: The startup-config is stored in NVRAM. It loads into RAM when the switch boots.
concepts.code:
SW1# show startup-config
! Boot configuration — lives in NVRAM

concepts.title: Saving & Restoring
concepts.body: Use "write memory" or "copy running-config startup-config" to save. Use "copy startup-config running-config" to restore.
concepts.code:
Save:   write memory
Restore: copy startup-config running-config
